title: Tenant Isolation: A CDN Serves Another Customer’s Invoice
businessContext: A SaaS invoice API authenticates at the origin, but a CDN rollout caches /api/invoices/42 by path alone. Different tenants use the same local invoice IDs, so cache hits can bypass origin authorization.
problemStatement: A customer reports an invoice bearing another company’s name. The response has X-Cache: Hit and Age: 83. Work through three timed developments, justify your actions, and write an evidence-based incident response. The simulation starts paused; advancing time can expire unanswered decisions.
constraints: Treat the report as a potential confidentiality incident and preserve access evidence.
Do not trust a client-supplied tenant header as authorization.
Use synthetic tenant fixtures for verification; do not expose more customer records while testing.
All telemetry is synthetic. Actions only affect this practice simulation.
candidateTasks: Contain customer impact while preserving evidence and data integrity.
Respond to each new development and explain the selected action.
Cite telemetry supporting the root cause; distinguish observation from inference.
Define a permanent correction, regression coverage, recovery gates, and stakeholder update.

hints: Tenant A MISS followed by tenant B HIT on the same path returns the same invoice.
Disable shared caching for private invoice paths through verified CDN policy, then invalidate affected objects.
Keep private invoice responses uncached with private, no-store semantics and a CDN configuration that respects them.
alternativeApproaches: Cache only public invoice-independent assets and retain private data access at the origin.
A separately reviewed edge authorization design may support private caching, but identity verification and cache partitioning must hold for every hit.
commonMistakes: Assuming correct origin authorization protects CDN cache hits.
Deleting evidence or closing the investigation after testing one customer path.
